text:
alex: heads-up — i'm seeing a perf regression in prod p99 after yesterday's kernel selector change. want to talk safe profiling approaches to pinning this down without blowing up latency or trace budgets :grimacing:

sophie: ugh. what signal do you have? increased latency with specific models? or wider tail?

alex: mostly p99 spikiness for text-gen routes on Dedicated hosts. baseline looks fine but intermittent 200-400ms extra on some requests. no obvious spike in cpu/gpu util.

ryan: could be kv-cache cold paths triggering different kernel shapes. does this correlate with prefix lengths or cached keys?

alex: good call — initial checks show higher incidence when kv-cache miss rate rises above ~8%. those requests also show more small kernels in the timeline.

maria: interesting. my theory: kernel selection fallback picks a smaller launch config for short sequences and we lose warp efficiency. that + more kernel launches -> higher enqueue latency.

devin: to be diagnostic we should run lightweight traces on canary fleet, not full nsys everywhere. nsys full-trace overhead kills 99s.

alex: agree. what's a safe plan? sampling vs full, window sizes, and kernel-level visibility needs to be balanced.

ryan: from our bench runs: full nsys with cuda+nvtx ~15% token-time overhead on A100 for 60s traces. selective CUPTI sampling we tested earlier sits ~1-3% if we only sample kernels (no memory ops). perfetto for host-side scheduling ~<1%.

sophie: so proposal: 1) enable CUPTI-based kernel sampling on 10% canary traffic for 5m windows, sampled every 30s; 2) occasionally run 60s full nsys on single reserved node off-peak to capture rare code paths; 3) route traces to a short retention bucket and auto-delete after 7d.

alex: that sounds reasonable. need guardrails: auto-disable sampling if p99 latency delta > 2% or error rate increases. also limit trace size to ~50MB/min.

devin: implemented guardrail idea before — we can put a runtime check in the profiler shim: if measured mean latency increase > configured threshold within the first 30s, flip to "off" and emit alert. config via env: `REDWOOD_PROFILER_MODE=light|heavy` and `PROFILER_MAX_LAT_PCT=2`.

maria: also add a kernel filter: only capture kernels longer than 10us and aggregate per-kernel-name counts. avoids noise from tiny housekeeping kernels. we already have mappings from cuLaunch to logical op names.

ryan: kv-cache correlation: add an annotation to traces for kv-cache hit/miss and prefix_len. e.g., `nvtxRangePush("kv:m:miss prefix=32")`. that will let us slice by cache state in trace viewer.

alex: good. can we estimate overhead of the light config? if CUPTI sampling at 1 sample/sec and kernel filter, I expect <2% overall on p99. need numbers for SRE sign-off.

devin: from lab: CUPTI-sampled workload (1/s) + NVTX tagging added ~1.1% p99 in heavy token churn test. full nsys 60s gave ~18% in same test. numbers vary by model and batch size.

sophie: let's record those as expected ranges and annotate the canary run metadata. i'll draft the runbook: steps to turn on, monitor dashboards (latency, errors, trace-size), and abort criteria.

alex: runbook + ops checklist please. also add fallback plan: if canary shows regression, auto-switch kernel selector to previous heuristic (we keep last-good in config).

maria: one more: for heavy-nsys captures, use a dedicated isolate node to avoid noisy neighbors and set `NSYS_CAPTURE_RANGE=compute,memcpy` to reduce unnecessary traces. command: ```nsys profile -o /tmp/prof.nsys --trace=cuda,memcpy,nvtx --duration 60s --target-pid $PID```

ryan: and for perfetto host traces: `perfetto --config host_sched_cfg.pbtxt -o host.pftrace` — low overhead, gives us scheduler latency and context switch correlation with kernel launches.

alex: great. who can implement the profiler-shim guardrail and the NVTX kv annotations?

devin: i can do the shim + env config changes. will add auto-disable and simple telemetry events. target: PR by EOD tomorrow.

maria: i'll add the NVTX annotations in the KV cache hot code path and kernel name mapping. will also add the kernel-duration filter. PR in next 24h.

sophie: i'll write the runbook + rollback steps and add the canary dashboard panels.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary profiler rollout to 10% traffic at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z (UTC). :rocket:

alex: thanks all. once we have initial canary numbers we'll re-evaluate whether to run a single full nsys capture on an isolate node. :thumbsup:
